:::{#rem-induction-why}
#### Why the two steps suffice

The base case gives $P(n_0)$.
The inductive step with $n = n_0 + 1$ then gives $P(n_0 + 1)$,
with $n = n_0 + 2$ it gives $P(n_0 + 2)$,
and so on:
each integer $n \ge n_0$ is reached
after $n - n_0$ uses of the inductive step.

When $P(n)$ is needed only for $n_0 \le n \le r$,
it is enough to show the inductive step for $n_0 < n \le r$;
the same chain then stops at $P(r)$.

:::
